title: Map contract error codes to named per-contract SDK errors
body:
<!-- liquivault-backlog:typed-errors -->

## Status

Partially completed in commit 9e8aa0e: `LiquiVaultTransactionError` (src/wallet/transactionError.ts) exposes the failing stage, the submitted hash, an `outcomeUnknown` flag and a numeric `contractCode` parsed from simulation errors. What remains is turning that number into something an application can act on.

## Context

`contractCode` is a bare number. The same number means different things per contract: 16 is `WithdrawalLocked` in the pool, while the registry and escrow have their own enums. Applications currently need to hard-code these values.

## Scope

- `src/wallet/transactionError.ts`, `src/wallet/rpc.ts`
- Error enums in liquivault-contracts: `contracts/liquidity_pool/src/errors.rs`, `contracts/invoice_registry/src/errors.rs`, `contracts/factoring_escrow/src/errors.rs`

## Suggested complexity

Medium; final Wave complexity is set by maintainers in the Drips app.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Exported typed error with transaction stage and contract code when reliably available.
- [x] Preserve the submitted hash and an explicit unknown-outcome indication on interrupted confirmation.
- [x] Do not classify pending/unknown execution as success or silently retry a write.
- [ ] Export per-contract error name maps (`PoolErrorCode`, `RegistryErrorCode`, `EscrowErrorCode`) that match the Rust enums, plus a helper that resolves `{ contract, code, name }` for a failed call.
- [ ] Add a test that fails if a Rust enum value and the TypeScript map diverge (for example, a checked-in fixture generated from the Rust source).
- [ ] Test at least one representative error per contract using real simulation error shapes, including an unknown code.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build`

## Participation

title: Expose an explicit restoration planning API
body:
<!-- liquivault-backlog:archival-planning -->

## Status

Completed. Commit d36c284 added read-only restoration planning, 6d603af the automatic-restoration integration, and ee755ea caller-authorized prepareFootprintRestoration/executeFootprintRestoration with rejection, failed-confirmation and success tests. Closing.

## Original context

Current protocols can automatically restore archived entries using simulation-provided restore lists. The SDK relies on official preparation for that path, but has no caller-visible planner for restoration costs or a tested manual fallback for oversized/operator-sponsored recovery.

## Scope

`src/wallet/rpc.ts`

## Suggested complexity

High; final Wave complexity is set by maintainers in the Drips app.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Expose restoration requirements, affected entries and cost information without signing, submitting or spending by surprise.
- [x] Test the normal Protocol 23+ automatic restore-list path. Provide explicit caller-authorized manual restoration only when needed, confirm it and rebuild the original call afterwards.
- [x] Test restoration-needed, rejected restoration, failed restoration and successful recovery.
- [x] Keep footprint/auth data tied to the selected network and document sequence/fee behavior.
